summary: The [2020-2025 national digital strategy lapsed at term](2026-02-13-tunisie-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation-complete), and what replaced it is a [chapter of the development plan](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030) rather than a strategy — a change of instrument type, not a renewal.
developments:
All three volumes of the plan's digital annex are held ([annex](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030)).

A ministerial council in February 2026 placed 192 projects under national follow-up and declared 2026 the launch year; what the base and outside commentary had called a national digital strategy is a plan chapter ([vision](2026-02-13-tunisie-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation-complete), [lapse](2026-02-13-tunisie-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation-complete)).

A further ministerial council was held under the head of government in August 2026, and the decisions taken are not itemised in the record held ([council](2026-08-21-pm-gov-tn-zenzri-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation)).

Naming the instrument type correctly matters: a plan chapter is approved by finance law and carries no separate delivery machinery of its own.

2026-08-28 — a head-of-government circular directed ministers, secretaries of state, heads of public enterprises and state controllers to adopt strategic action plans on the governance and performance of public establishments, invoking among its legal bases the 2020 decree-law on electronic data exchange between public bodies ([circular](2026-08-28-tunisie-circulaire-pm-04-2026-gouvernance-entreprises-publiques)). A circular is a third instrument type in this space, below a plan chapter and below a strategy, and it is the one that actually names addressees and a duty.

summary: Outlines of a [national artificial-intelligence strategy](2026-08-15-tunisia-conseil-ministeriel-restreint-interoperabilite-tunisienumerique) were presented to a restricted ministerial council in August 2026 and drew a published sovereignty critique, and the strategy text is not held.
developments:
The outlines went to a restricted council on 16 August 2026 and a critique appeared the next day; a publications ranking circulating alongside it is a research-output measure and not evidence of state capability ([outlines](2026-08-15-tunisia-conseil-ministeriel-restreint-interoperabilite-tunisienumerique), [critique](2026-08-17-tunisia-ai-strategy-digital-sovereignty-critique-economiste-maghrebin), [ranking](2026-08-15-tunisia-ai-strategy-2026-2030-top-30-scientific-publications), [council](2026-08-16-tunisia-khadamet-digital-transformation-114-projects)).

A white paper on artificial intelligence was published open source by a diaspora association and presented at a global forum ([white paper](2026-08-05-intelligence-artificielle-latuge-devoile-son-livre-blanc-pour-la-tunisie), [forum](2026-07-22-tgf-2026-livre-blanc-ia)).

The country chairs an Arab working group on artificial-intelligence innovation while its own strategy is at outline stage and unpublished.

summary: A [draft organic law on personal data protection](2025-07-14-arp-tunisie-loi-organique-095-2025-protection-donnees-personnelles) was deposited in July 2025 and reached committee hearings in February 2026, to replace the [2004 organic law](2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament) still governing.
developments:
The bill was deposited on 14 July 2025, referred to the rights and liberties committee two days later, and heard in committee in February 2026 ([deposit](2025-07-14-arp-tunisie-loi-organique-095-2025-protection-donnees-personnelles), [hearings](2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament), [update](2026-06-23 Bimonthly Update on Privacy in Africa (January & February 2026))).

The tabled Arabic text is held from the Assembly's own dossier and its article count is settled from it at 132: a committee account giving 123 reads as a transposition whose six-part structure matches the tabled text section for section, and a third account's 32 is a leading-digit loss in optical transcription. Whether the committee has since shortened the bill is not established.

The 2004 law was still the governing instrument when the replacement entered committee ([law](2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament), [rights](2024-04-01 Londa 2023 Digital Rights and Inclusion in Africa - Tunisia (Paradigm Initiative))).

summary: [Organic laws on biometric identity](2024-03-07 Eight years in the making - Tunisia's Biometric ID and Passport Bills risk rights) were adopted in March 2024, and civil society records that committee deliberations lacked public consultation.
developments:
The laws were adopted by parliament on 6 March 2024, with use of the biometric card and passport targeted for the first half of 2025 ([laws](2024-03-07 Eight years in the making - Tunisia's Biometric ID and Passport Bills risk rights), [usage](2024-04-23 Tunisia - Biometric ID card and passport usage to begin in H1 2025), [rollout](2024-04-23 Tunisia to Get Biometric IDs in H1 of 2025)).

The consultation criticism is an attributed position rather than a finding of this report.

Two and a half years on, whether issuance has begun is recorded separately as not established — so the enabling statutes are in force and their effect is unmeasured.

summary: The [Development Plan 2026-2030 was promulgated as a law](2026-07-23-tunisie-loi-2026-16-approbation-plan-de-developpement-2026-2030) in July 2026, and every volume of the annex held is marked draft.
developments:
It was promulgated on 20 July 2026 after adoption by both chambers ([law](2026-07-23-tunisie-loi-2026-16-approbation-plan-de-developpement-2026-2030), [annex](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030)).

Whether the promulgated annex differs from the version tabled and voted is not established, and no as-enacted printing has been published. That is a live problem rather than a formality: the annex is where the digital programme's project lines sit, so the legally binding content of the country's digital plan cannot be read.

summary: The [national data-protection authority](2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament) was cited by the replacement bill's own sponsors as institutionally limited.
developments:
The characterisation is the sponsors', made in February 2026 as part of the case for the new organic law ([authority](2026-02-20-africanmanager-data-protection-law-parliament)).

No enforcement action, penalty, complaint volume or registration figure for the authority is published at any date. A legislature's own sponsors naming the regulator as the reason for replacing the statute is the strongest statement about it in the record.

summary: No [legal basis is held for the linked national health dataset](2026-07-27-assabahnews-moarref-watani-sihi-sahetna) joining health, civil-status, social-affairs and education records; the ministry asserts only that data is stored confidentially and securely.
developments:
What is missing is a decree, ministerial order or data-sharing instrument stating the basis, retention rule and supervisory authority for that dataset ([basis](2026-07-27-assabahnews-moarref-watani-sihi-sahetna)).

The dataset it would govern is live: the national health identifier is the repurposed vaccination identifier, the health portal has passed technical validation and a cybersecurity audit, and a digital birth declaration is running at one hospital.

An assertion of confidentiality is not a legal basis, and the statute that would supply one is the 2004 law the government is replacing.

summary: The country [took a continental telecommunications union council seat](2026-07-26-assabahnews-tunisia-atu-council-2027-2030) and [chairs an Arab artificial-intelligence working group](2026-08-01-egypt-chairs-58th-aticm-executive-bureau-arab-ai-groups), and hosted the [ninth Arab civil-status conference](2026-08-20-ahram-tawsiyat-mutamar-arabi-jinsiya-ahwal-madaniya).
developments:
The council seat was won at a plenipotentiary conference in July 2026 ([seat](2026-07-26-assabahnews-tunisia-atu-council-2027-2030)), and the working-group chair was taken at an Arab permanent committee's inaugural meeting held in the capital, with only the month published for the election date ([chair](2026-08-01-egypt-chairs-58th-aticm-executive-bureau-arab-ai-groups)).

The civil-status conference closed in the capital in August 2026 with recommendations only: no instrument is adopted, no member-state commitment is stated and the model framework itself is not held ([conference](2026-08-20-ahram-tawsiyat-mutamar-arabi-jinsiya-ahwal-madaniya)).

Three regional positions taken in two months, none of which produces an obligation the base can read.

summary: The [1989 Maghreb Union treaty](1989-02-17-uma-treaty-instituting-arab-maghreb-union) is in force with a binding judicial organ and no summit since 1994.
developments:
The [treaty concluded at Marrakesh in February 1989](1989-02-17-uma-treaty-instituting-arab-maghreb-union) has been in force since 1 July 1989 and establishes a presidential council, a council of foreign ministers, a general secretariat, a consultative council and a judicial organ whose rulings bind.

No summit has been held since 1994, so the instrument supplies a legal frame for harmonisation and no working machinery. Harmonisation between Maghreb states therefore proceeds bilaterally where it proceeds at all.

summary: The [twentieth mutual recognition working group with Libya](2025-12-18-lncsm-libya-tunisia-mutual-recognition-task-force-20th-meeting) concluded in December 2025.
developments:
The [meeting concluded in December 2025](2025-12-18-lncsm-libya-tunisia-mutual-recognition-task-force-20th-meeting) is the twentieth of a standing bilateral working group on the mutual recognition of conformity certificates and the quality and conformity marks.

It is the base's only record of Tunisian conformity assessment being recognised across a border, and it runs bilaterally rather than through the regional treaty, which has [held no summit since 1994](1989-02-17-uma-treaty-instituting-arab-maghreb-union).

summary: No [appropriation line for the digital programme](2026-08-04-sara-zaafrani-zenzri-devoile-les-grandes-orientations-du-projet-de-loi-de-finances-2027) is held; the 2027 draft names acceleration of the digital transition as a structuring axis with no allocation, target or named programme attached.
developments:
What is missing is an appropriation line in the 2027 finance law or the 2026 budget showing what the state spends on the digital programme ([orientations](2026-08-04-sara-zaafrani-zenzri-devoile-les-grandes-orientations-du-projet-de-loi-de-finances-2027)).

That absence sits against 192 projects under national follow-up, 114 in execution, 34 service houses built and an interoperability platform in its second phase. The delivery is countable and the money behind it is not.

summary: [Telecommunications cooperation with a neighbour](2026-06-09-algeria-tunisia-telecom-ict-cooperation--techafricanews) was announced, and [minutes were signed for a triangular startup programme with Japan](2026-07-28-tunisie-japon-jica-s2t-partenariat-ecosysteme-startups-africain) serving other African states.
developments:
The bilateral cooperation was announced in June 2026 with no instrument, value or workstream stated ([cooperation](2026-06-09-algeria-tunisia-telecom-ict-cooperation--techafricanews)).

The triangular programme's minutes were signed in July 2026; the country's own startup framework is the curriculum, so what it exports is a policy design rather than a technology ([programme](2026-07-28-tunisie-japon-jica-s2t-partenariat-ecosysteme-startups-africain)).

Exporting a startup statute as a curriculum for other states is unusual in this frame and worth recording as the form the relationship takes.

summary: A [EUR 190m loan to the state operator](2026-01-16-ebrd-tunisie-telecom-190m-medusa) is the lender's first public-sector project in the country without a sovereign guarantee since 2012, and a [European grant for the cable segment](2024-12-03-ec-cef-digital-viatunisia-project-record) closed in August 2025.
developments:
The loan was publicly announced in January 2026 after board approval in July 2024, with interest tied to sustainability and state-enterprise reform milestones ([loan](2026-01-16-ebrd-tunisie-telecom-190m-medusa), [board](2024-07-24-ebrd-board-report-project-hannibal-tunisie-telecom), [record](2024-07-24-ebrd-tun-2024-tunisie-telecom-project-hannibal-bw01)).

The cable grant's project period closed on 31 August 2025; the Commission's record states no grant-agreement signature date, and a December 2022 signing carried by trade press is not supported by it ([grant](2024-12-03-ec-cef-digital-viatunisia-project-record), [project](2023-01-01-european-union-tun-2023-viatunisia-cef-digital-bw02)).

An earlier economic and social reforms grant is discontinued ([reforms](2016-09-01-iati-46002-g-tn-i00-zzz-002-tunisia-economic-social-reforms-inclusive-growth)). Interest tied to reform milestones, on an unguaranteed loan to a state operator, is the sharpest conditionality in this ledger.

summary: All three operators [launched fifth-generation service within days of each other](2025-02-17-developingtelecoms-three-operators-launch-5g) in February 2025, on a market where [mobile broadband is the dominant access point](2026-03-09-telecomreviewafrica-north-africa-digital-generation).
developments:
The three launches came within days in February 2025, and independent measurement of speed a year on is a reference study cited rather than absorbed as country state ([launch](2025-02-17-developingtelecoms-three-operators-launch-5g), [measurement](2026-08-03-ookla-5g-north-africa-one-year-on)).

Regulator data shows mobile broadband as the dominant access point ([market](2026-03-09-telecomreviewafrica-north-africa-digital-generation), [growth](2025-04-11-techafricanews-telecom-data-driven-growth)).

Three simultaneous launches indicate a coordinated award rather than competitive timing, and no spectrum award document is held.

summary: The regulator published an [affordability report on international data](2026-07-18-tunisie-internet-abordabilite) in July 2026, cited as a reference measurement rather than absorbed.
developments:
It is cited as a reference measurement, not absorbed as country state ([report](2026-07-18-tunisie-internet-abordabilite)).

A regulator publishing an affordability comparison is the kind of measurement most units in this frame lack entirely, and this base holds the fact of it rather than its figures.

summary: A [submarine cable landing became ready for service](2026-06-26-techafricanews-orange-medusa-cable-operational) in June 2026, with the state operator holding a [dedicated fibre pair](2026-06-05-connectingafrica-viatunisia-subsea-live) on it.
developments:
The landing was ready for service on 3 June 2026. Both national operators' publicity claimed the landing; it is settled against the cable operator's own newsroom, which makes one the owner and the other a capacity customer ([operational](2026-06-26-techafricanews-orange-medusa-cable-operational), [live](2026-06-05-connectingafrica-viatunisia-subsea-live), [landing](2025-11-01-medusa-lands-in-bizerte), [hosting](2023-05-11-orange-tunisia-medusa-bizerte-hosting-agreement)).

The state operator's dedicated pair entered service with the cable; the cable operator's record gives it as 20 Tbps and trade press and a national re-report give 22 ([pair](2026-06-05-connectingafrica-viatunisia-subsea-live), [joining](2025-02-10-tunisie-telecom-joins-medusa-fibre-pair)).

Two operators claiming one landing, and two capacity figures for one fibre pair, are both settled here against the operator of the cable.

summary: A [satellite licence is withheld](2026-06-13-tunisia-starlink-status-check-carthage) with pre-orders opened in February 2026, the unresolved point being routing through a local ground station and a national interconnection point.
developments:
Pre-orders opened in February 2026 with no licence issued ([status](2026-06-13-tunisia-starlink-status-check-carthage), [pre-orders](2026-02-16-tunisia-starlink-precommandes-licence-thd)).

The unresolved point is routing: the state wants low-earth-orbit traffic through a local ground station and a national interconnection point.

That is a substantive sovereignty position rather than an administrative delay, and it is stated more clearly here than in any other unit in this frame that has withheld or granted the same licence.

summary: [Data centres are a named project line](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030) in the development plan annex, and a [non-binding memorandum](2026-02-06-dcd-solecrypt-schneider-bizerte-data-center) was signed for a facility at a coastal city.
developments:
The plan annex carries data centres as a state investment priority ([plan](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030), [strategy](2025-10-15-trendsnafrica-tia-data-centers-strategy)).

The memorandum with an equipment supplier is non-binding and was signed in February 2026 ([memorandum](2026-02-06-dcd-solecrypt-schneider-bizerte-data-center)).

No operating capacity, utilisation or facility count for the country appears anywhere in this ledger, so the priority is stated and the estate is unmeasured.

summary: The health ministry confirmed an [intention to adopt domestic cloud solutions](2026-02-13 Tunisia Advances Digital Health Reform With AI and National Cloud Strategy) for national health data.
developments:
The confirmation came in February 2026 ([intention](2026-02-13 Tunisia Advances Digital Health Reform With AI and National Cloud Strategy)).

No provider, capacity, procurement or timetable is named. The dataset it would host is the linked health record for which no legal basis is held, so the sovereignty question and the lawfulness question are both open on the same data.

summary: A developer's [solar site for data-centre power](2026-02-06-dcd-solecrypt-schneider-bizerte-data-center) was at base-camp stage in November 2025.
developments:
It reaches the base through the same account as the data-centre memorandum ([site](2026-02-06-dcd-solecrypt-schneider-bizerte-data-center)).

No capacity, commissioning date or connection arrangement is stated. It is the only energy item in this ledger, and it belongs to a private developer rather than to the state.

summary: A [head-of-government circular of 2 September 2026](2026-09-05-lapresse-tunisia-cybersecurity-analysis) sets a security baseline across public sites, platforms and state messaging; the agency itself [publishes advisories and no incident statistics](2026-07-30-ansi-tunisia-phishing-sms-warning).
developments:
Circular n. 5 of 2 September 2026 requires [encrypted connections, mandatory renewal of security certificates, two-factor verification for administrator access, protection against traffic-saturation attacks and hosting on state-approved servers, bans the use of messaging apps and social media for official documents, and requires regular audits, immediate reporting to the national cybersecurity agency and an end to shared credentials](2026-09-05-lapresse-tunisia-cybersecurity-analysis). It binds the administration, not the wider economy, and carries no compliance deadline, audit schedule or list of approved hosts.

The advisory on a short-message phishing campaign was issued in July 2026 ([advisory](2026-07-30-ansi-tunisia-phishing-sms-warning)).

The attack and ransomware figures come from the interior ministry and the agency, cover different periods and are not a series; no definition of a recorded attack and no incident-reporting obligation behind the count is stated ([figures](2026-08-07-tunisia-cyberattacks-ransomware-surge-economiste-maghrebin)).

An agency that publishes consumer advisories and no incident statistics of its own is the readiness position here.

summary: A [second-phase contract for the national interoperability platform](2026-05-14-cybernetica-national-interoperability-platform-phase2) was signed in May 2026.
developments:
The platform has been in place since 2024 and entered a second phase under contract in May 2026 ([phase two](2026-05-14-cybernetica-national-interoperability-platform-phase2), [platform](2024-02-14 National interoperability platform in Tunisia (Cybernetica UXP))).

No connected-agency count, transaction volume or governing instrument is published. It is the layer the health identifier, the business register, the social registry and the service portal would all have to cross, and none of those cells can state whether it does.

summary: Whether [issuance of the biometric card and passport has begun](2024-04-23 Tunisia - Biometric ID card and passport usage to begin in H1 2025) is not established, two and a half years after the enabling laws and past the targeted date.
developments:
What is missing is an interior ministry statement, an issuance figure or a gazette notice. The enabling organic laws passed in March 2024 and use was targeted for the first half of 2025; nothing held states whether issuance has begun ([target](2024-04-23 Tunisia - Biometric ID card and passport usage to begin in H1 2025), [bills](2024-03-07 Eight years in the making - Tunisia's Biometric ID and Passport Bills risk rights)).

Interior ministry figures for identity and travel documents issued through digital services were given in August 2026 as a ministry statement rather than a published series, with the passport figure given as several thousand without a number ([figures](2026-08-18-lapresse-tn-modernisation-administrative-passeports-cin)).

A biometric credential programme eight years in the making, whose issuance cannot be confirmed either way, is the gap at the centre of this unit's identity record.

summary: The [mobile identity credential became compulsory](2026-06-26-techafricanews-mobile-id-mandatory-investors) for investment declarations and business registration from 1 July 2026 — two public-service rails switching on the same date.
developments:
It was made compulsory for investment declarations and for business registration from 1 July 2026 ([mandate](2026-06-26-techafricanews-mobile-id-mandatory-investors), [register](2026-04-27-africanmanager-national-business-register-digital), [milestone](2025-03-19 E-Houwiya - A Milestone in Tunisia's Digital Transformation Roadmap 2025 (ID Tech))).

Two independent public-service rails switched to compulsory digital identity on the same date, which is a coordination decision rather than two coincidences.

No enrolment count, coverage figure or fallback for a user without the credential is published, and the mobile application announced for government services depends on this same identity layer.

summary: The [national health identifier](2026-07-27-assabahnews-moarref-watani-sihi-sahetna) is the repurposed Covid-19 vaccination identifier, and a [single social identifier](2026-08-19-presidence-gouvernement-tunisie-reforme-securite-sociale) was worked on at a ministerial session in August 2026.
developments:
The health identifier was confirmed as the repurposed vaccination identifier in July 2026; three counts circulate at three scopes and do not contradict each other, no national coverage figure has been published and no public dashboard exists ([identifier](2026-07-27-assabahnews-moarref-watani-sihi-sahetna), [pilot](2026-07-15-tmo-national-health-identifier-pilot), [portal](2026-07-23-tunisia-finalizes-sahetna-digital-health-portal-national-id)).

The social identifier sits inside the health half of a wider social-security reform decision, on the government's own communique ([social](2026-08-19-presidence-gouvernement-tunisie-reforme-securite-sociale)).

Repurposing a pandemic identifier as the permanent health identifier is a decision about scope that no published instrument governs, which is the same gap the health dataset's missing legal basis names.

summary: The central bank [launched a national payment label](2026-05-07-wearetech-central-bank-tunpay-label) with the national payments operator, [licensed an operator fintech wallet](2026-03-07-menastartupdigest-ooredoo-walletii-license), and the state operator [launched a wallet](2026-03-18-assabah-tunisie-telecom-kashy-wallet) of its own.
developments:
The payment label was launched in May 2026 with the national payments operator ([label](2026-05-07-wearetech-central-bank-tunpay-label)).

An operator fintech wallet received its central bank licence in March 2026 ([licence](2026-03-07-menastartupdigest-ooredoo-walletii-license)), and the state operator launched a wallet in the same month; the base's capture of the only source no longer carries the article, so the launch detail is not currently citable beyond the headline ([wallet](2026-03-18-assabah-tunisie-telecom-kashy-wallet)).

Two operator wallets licensed or launched in one month, under a new national label, is a coordinated opening of the payments market rather than three separate events.

summary: [Mobile payments rose 81 per cent](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025) in 2025 on central bank figures, and the [active wallet count](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025) diverges by a factor of about 1.7 between two reporting routes.
developments:
The postal operator provided digital wallets free to students for the 2026-2027 university registration ([report](2026-08-31-lapresse-tunisia-laposte-etudiants-wallets)). No take-up figure is stated.

The mobile payment and licensed-provider figures are the central bank's full-year 2025 numbers, reaching the base through an aggregator's repackaging rather than the bulletin itself ([payments](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025), [providers](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025)).

The base carries 815,000 wallets for 2025 from that aggregator ([wallets](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025)); reporting attributed directly to the bulletins gives roughly 469,000 at end-2025, and only the aggregator's side is held ([wallets](2026-02-23 Central Bank Of Tunisia Reports 81% Surge In Mobile Payments As Tunisia Accelerates Its Digital Transformation In 2025)).

A near-doubling in mobile payments and a wallet count that differs by 1.7 times between routes cannot both be read confidently, and the divergence is stated rather than resolved.

summary: A published analysis finds [no rule allocating the loss](2026-08-09-tunisia-cyber-risk-electronic-payments-liability-gap) between bank, merchant and cardholder when an electronic payment is hijacked or blocked by a cyber incident.
developments:
The analysis checks the 2000 electronic commerce law, the 2023 cybersecurity decree-law and the central bank's 2024 circular and finds no text allocating the loss ([analysis](2026-08-09-tunisia-cyber-risk-electronic-payments-liability-gap)).

It sets that against a payments market of 164.8 million transactions worth 29.5bn dinars in 2025, up 12.3 per cent, and reported cyber incidents rising from 63,000 in 2021 to more than 155,000 in 2022 ([market](2026-08-09-tunisia-cyber-risk-electronic-payments-liability-gap)).

A market of that size with no loss-allocation rule is the same gap SLE records, and here it is identified by a legal analysis rather than by a fraud wave.

summary: A [digital birth declaration platform](2026-06-11-alchourouk-digital-birth-declaration-pilot) is running at one hospital, with 202 births registered.
developments:
The interior ministry launched remote issuance of birth certificates through the national services platform ([launch](2026-08-31-lapresse-tunisia-birth-cert-remote)), with a remote translation service alongside it ([report](2026-08-31-radionationale-tunisia-birth-cert-remote-translation)).

It is the first national platform of its kind and is running at a single hospital ([platform](2026-06-11-alchourouk-digital-birth-declaration-pilot), [pilot](2026-07-27-assabahnews-moarref-watani-sihi-sahetna)).

Two hundred and two births is a pilot volume, and no rollout plan, second site or completion date is published. The country hosted the Arab conference of civil-status directors in the same month.

summary: [Paper filing at the national business register was discontinued](2026-04-27-africanmanager-national-business-register-digital) from 1 July 2026 under a February decree, and a [register of community companies](2026-07-23-tunisie-registre-national-des-societes-communautaires-alahlia) launched in July.
developments:
Paper filing ended on 1 July 2026 under the finance minister's decree of 12 February ([register](2026-04-27-africanmanager-national-business-register-digital)).

That is the same date the mobile identity credential became compulsory for business registration, so the paper channel closed and the digital credential became mandatory together.

A national register of community companies launched on 20 July 2026 under a 2025 decree-law ([community](2026-07-23-tunisie-registre-national-des-societes-communautaires-alahlia)).

summary: The [social registry](2024-11-14 Tunisians Share How their Life Changed Through the AMEN Program) carried more than 333,000 households on cash transfers as of December 2023, and a [social housing application platform](2026-08-04-logements-sociaux-en-tunisie-une-plateforme-numerique-pour-accelerer-les-demandes-daccession-a-la-propriete) has beneficiary-database interconnection still under way.
developments:
The registry figure is from December 2023 and nothing later is held ([registry](2024-11-14 Tunisians Share How their Life Changed Through the AMEN Program), [nexus](2020-01-01 Nexus between Civil Registration and Social Protection - Tunisia chapter (IDRC))).

The housing platform's completion timetable was set at a follow-up meeting in August 2026, with beneficiary-database interconnection still under way ([housing](2026-08-04-logements-sociaux-en-tunisie-une-plateforme-numerique-pour-accelerer-les-demandes-daccession-a-la-propriete)).

A social identifier is separately being worked on inside a social-security reform, so three social-data systems are in motion and none states how it relates to the others.

summary: The [national health portal](2026-07-23-tunisia-finalizes-sahetna-digital-health-portal-national-id) completed technical validation and a cybersecurity audit in July 2026, and a [digital hospital project](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030) is carried in the plan with telemedicine and imaging first.
developments:
Technical validation and the cybersecurity audit were reported complete on 21 July 2026 ([portal](2026-07-23-tunisia-finalizes-sahetna-digital-health-portal-national-id), [platform](2026-07-24-tunisie-plateforme-sanitaire-numerique-ma-sante)).

The digital hospital project is a plan line with telemedicine and imaging first ([hospital](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030), [council](2026-02-13-tunisie-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation-complete)).

A completed cybersecurity audit is more than most systems in this frame can show. The legal basis for the linked dataset the portal serves is separately recorded as not held, so the technical assurance is ahead of the legal one.

summary: A [school life platform](2026-08-06-tunisia-education-ministry-digital-school-life-platform) was launched in August 2026, and its legal basis and relationship to an [earlier education platform](2024-01-08 Tunisia Unveils Digital Platform to Boost Education Transparency, Equity) are not stated.
developments:
The platform was announced by ministry communique on 6 August 2026, and neither its legal basis nor its relationship to the 2024 education platform is stated ([platform](2026-08-06-tunisia-education-ministry-digital-school-life-platform)).

The earlier platform was launched in January 2024 to improve education transparency and equity ([earlier](2024-01-08 Tunisia Unveils Digital Platform to Boost Education Transparency, Equity)).

Two ministry education platforms with no stated relationship is the same unreconciled-systems pattern the social-data cells show.

summary: [Online business tax registration](2026-08-04-patente-en-ligne-la-direction-generale-des-impots-lance-sa-nouvelle-plateforme-numerique) was deployed by the tax directorate, a [wholesale-markets electronic invoicing programme](2026-08-03-la-sotumag-poursuit-la-mise-en-oeuvre-du-programme-national-de-generalisation-du-systeme-de-facturation-electronique) completed a pilot, and a [compulsory e-invoicing amendment](2026-02-10-assabah-parliament-e-invoicing-law-amendment) is in joint committee.
developments:
The tax registration platform was announced in August 2026 ([registration](2026-08-04-patente-en-ligne-la-direction-generale-des-impots-lance-sa-nouvelle-plateforme-numerique)).

The wholesale-markets programme completed a pilot at one market with an official launch at a second set for August 2026; it runs through the state wholesale-markets company under the trade ministry, and its relationship to the compulsory e-invoicing amendment is not stated in either source ([programme](2026-08-03-la-sotumag-poursuit-la-mise-en-oeuvre-du-programme-national-de-generalisation-du-systeme-de-facturation-electronique)).

The amendment bill was debated in joint committee in February 2026 ([amendment](2026-02-10-assabah-parliament-e-invoicing-law-amendment)). A sector programme generalising electronic invoicing while the statute mandating it is still in committee is the sequence, and no source connects them.

summary: An [electronic rules-of-origin system](2026-08-18-lapresse-tn-douane-systeme-tuniso-coreen-regles-origine) opened its execution phase, with technical preparation running to September 2026.
developments:
The execution phase opened in August 2026 with technical preparation to 18 September ([system](2026-08-18-lapresse-tn-douane-systeme-tuniso-coreen-regles-origine)).

No go-live date, trader-facing interface or cost is published. It is a bilateral technical cooperation rather than a domestic build, and the customs administration's wider systems do not appear in this ledger.

summary: [Thirty-four digital service houses](2026-08-14-tunisia-34-digital-service-houses-21-governorates) were completed across 21 governorates in seven months, and the [project portfolio is counted as 114 in execution and 192 under tracking](2026-08-17-tunisia-pm-gov-interconnection-digitalisation-decision) with no reconciliation published.
developments:
A first version of the national services application launched, giving citizens unified round-the-clock access to electronic services ([launch](2026-08-31-lapresse-tunisia-khadamet-launch)), and a unified platform came into service as the single gateway to the industry ministry's services ([platform](2026-08-28-lapresse-tunisia-eindustrie-platform)).

The service houses were completed between December 2025 and June 2026; the reach figure is the programme's own and counts citizens reached rather than transactions completed, and no service list or staffing model is stated ([houses](2026-08-14-tunisia-34-digital-service-houses-21-governorates)).

The two project counts measure different things — 114 in execution against 192 under national tracking — and the government publishes no reconciliation, project list or completion series for either ([portfolio](2026-08-17-tunisia-pm-gov-interconnection-digitalisation-decision), [projects](2026-08-16-tunisia-khadamet-digital-transformation-114-projects), [review](2026-08-15-tunisia-114-digital-transformation-projects-cabinet-review)).

A single administrative services portal was reported delivered by end-2025 ([portal](2026-02-13-tunisie-conseil-ministeriel-digitalisation-complete)), and a mobile application announced for imminent launch sits on top of that existing portal rather than replacing it, depending on the mobile identity credential ([application](2026-08-16-tunisia-khadamet-digital-transformation-114-projects)).

The industry ministry opened a unified digital services platform on 28 August 2026, its first service the technical cards governing effective transfer operations - more than 4,000 a year - filed and processed entirely online and interconnected with customs so data is exchanged and decisions notified in real time ([platform](2026-08-28-alchourouk-industry-ministry-digital-platform)). It runs on the national digital identity mechanisms and is linked to the enterprise register, with import authorisations and establishment licences to follow on a phased timetable.

summary: [Immediate procurement to complete a technology park](2026-08-10-tunisia-cite-numerique-ennahli-grands-projets-acceleration) was ordered in August 2026, and a [digital summit](2026-04-22-assabah-tunisia-digital-summit-10) held its tenth edition.
developments:
No cost, completion date, occupancy plan or account of why the park was incomplete is stated ([park](2026-08-10-tunisia-cite-numerique-ennahli-grands-projets-acceleration)).

The summit reached its tenth edition in April 2026 ([summit](2026-04-22-assabah-tunisia-digital-summit-10)).

An order for immediate procurement to finish a park, with no explanation of the delay, is the only thing published about it.

summary: The [startup statute and its national programme](2026-07-28-tunisie-japon-jica-s2t-partenariat-ecosysteme-startups-africain) were adopted as the curriculum of a Japanese-financed programme for other African states.
developments:
The adoption was reported in July 2026 ([curriculum](2026-07-28-tunisie-japon-jica-s2t-partenariat-ecosysteme-startups-africain)).

No domestic figure — labelled companies, funding raised, jobs — appears anywhere in this ledger. A framework being exported as a model while its own outcomes go unmeasured at home is what the record supports.

summary: [Digital skills are named in the plan annex](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030) approved by law in July 2026, and a [first cohort of 100 women entrepreneurs](2026-08-19-assabahnews-escwa-women-entrepreneurs-ecommerce-ai-training) opened in August.
developments:
The skills line is named in the plan annex ([skills](2026-06-01-tunisie-plan-developpement-2026-2030)), with no target, budget or programme attached in anything held.

The women entrepreneurs cohort opened in August 2026 with the training launch's own date not established in the source ([cohort](2026-08-19-assabahnews-escwa-women-entrepreneurs-ecommerce-ai-training)).

One cohort of a hundred is the entire delivered training record for this country in the period.

summary: The regulator's observatory published a [one-page synthesis of its 2026 internet and digital skills survey](2026-07-24-int-tunisie-synthese-enquete-internet-competences-numeriques-2026), and the full report is not published.
developments:
The synthesis carries no printed date and is dated from the earliest press report of its publication. The full survey report — sample design, fieldwork dates, question wording — is not published, and the observatory has issued full report documents for 2023, 2021 and 2019 but only this synthesis for 2026 ([synthesis](2026-07-24-int-tunisie-synthese-enquete-internet-competences-numeriques-2026), [survey](2026-07-27-tunisie-enquete-int-2026-usage-internet-competences-numeriques)).

Use of online public administration comes from the same survey ([e-government](2026-07-28-tunisie-enquete-observatoire-int-2026-ia-achats-en-ligne)).

A statistical series that has published full reports for three previous rounds and a single page for this one is a regression in transparency rather than in measurement, and it is the source under this report's usage figures.

summary: A [national public data registry](2026-08-04-tunisia-results-report-2023-2025) is confirmed live and enabling citizen data requests, and an [agrifood sector data portal](2026-07-23-tunisie-portail-industries-agroalimentaires-lancement) launched in July 2026.
developments:
The registry's live status is a finding of an independent review mechanism's report published in August 2026, cited for that specific finding rather than absorbed in full; the registry's own launch date is not given ([registry](2026-08-04-tunisia-results-report-2023-2025)).

The agrifood portal launched on 23 July 2026 after a full functional test two weeks earlier ([portal](2026-07-23-tunisie-portail-industries-agroalimentaires-lancement), [launch](2026-07-26-tunisie-portail-agroalimentaire-veille-economique-giz)).

A femicide data platform was announced for launch in August 2026 by a non-governmental organisation, included here because it is the country's gender-based-violence data infrastructure and the state has none ([femicide](2026-08-10-tunisia-aswat-nissa-femicide-platform-wearetech)).
